soru: Büyük dil modellerinin eğitim verisinde belirli bir metnin yer alıp almadığını tespit etme (üyelik çıkarımı) ve test verisi kirlenmesi üzerine en önemli çalışmalar, güvenlik sonuçları ve açık problemler neler?
istem:
Research question: Büyük dil modellerinin eğitim verisinde belirli bir metnin yer alıp almadığını tespit etme (üyelik çıkarımı) ve test verisi kirlenmesi üzerine en önemli çalışmalar, güvenlik sonuçları ve açık problemler neler?

Cutoff date: 2026-04-21. Only works published BEFORE this date count.

List the 30 most important works (papers) for this research question that were published before the cutoff date, in order of importance (most important first), each with its arXiv id and/or DOI. You may search the web.

When you are done, reply with ONLY a JSON object in this form (no other text):
{"calismalar": [{"sira": 1, "baslik": "exact title", "yil": 2020, "arxiv_id": "arXiv id or null", "doi": "DOI or null", "gerekce": "one sentence on why this work is important"}]}
with exactly 30 items. If you do not know an identifier, use null instead of guessing.

calismalar.baslik: Membership Inference Attacks against Machine Learning Models
calismalar.gerekce: This paper defined the membership inference attack and introduced the shadow-model method that all later work on detecting training data builds on.

calismalar.baslik: Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It showed that verbatim training data can be extracted from GPT-2 and used membership-inference signals to rank candidates, making LLM privacy risk concrete.

calismalar.baslik: Detecting Pretraining Data from Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It introduced the Min-K% Prob method and the WikiMIA benchmark, which became the standard baseline for reference-free detection of pretraining data.

calismalar.baslik: Do Membership Inference Attacks Work on Large Language Models?
calismalar.gerekce: Its MIMIR benchmark showed that membership inference on LLMs often performs near chance when the train/test distributions are properly matched.

calismalar.baslik: Membership Inference Attacks From First Principles
calismalar.gerekce: It introduced the LiRA attack and evaluation by true-positive rate at low false-positive rates, which set the methodological standard for the field.

calismalar.baslik: Quantifying Memorization Across Neural Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It showed that memorization grows log-linearly with model size, data duplication and context length.

calismalar.baslik: Proving Test Set Contamination in Black Box Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It provides a black-box statistical test for test-set contamination, based on how likely the model finds the original ordering of benchmark examples.

calismalar.baslik: Blind Baselines Beat Membership Inference Attacks for Foundation Models
calismalar.gerekce: It showed that blind baselines that never query the model beat the published attacks, exposing distribution shift in the evaluation datasets.

calismalar.baslik: SoK: Membership Inference Attacks on LLMs are Rushing Nowhere (and How to Fix It)
calismalar.gerekce: It systematizes the flawed post-hoc evaluation setups in LLM membership inference and proposes randomized test designs.

calismalar.baslik: Time Travel in LLMs: Tracing Data Contamination in Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It introduced guided-instruction prompting to detect contamination at the instance and partition level.

calismalar.baslik: NLP Evaluation in trouble: On the Need to Measure LLM Data Contamination for each Benchmark
calismalar.gerekce: This position paper made data contamination a central problem for reliable NLP evaluation.

calismalar.baslik: Membership Inference Attacks against Language Models via Neighbourhood Comparison
calismalar.gerekce: It proposed a reference-model-free attack that compares a text's loss with the losses of its neighbor texts.

calismalar.baslik: Min-K%++: Improved Baseline for Detecting Pre-Training Data from Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It improved Min-K% with normalized token scores based on local-maximum detection, giving a stronger baseline.

calismalar.baslik: LLM Dataset Inference: Did you train on my dataset?
calismalar.gerekce: It moved the problem from single examples to whole datasets, enabling statistically significant detection for copyright claims.

calismalar.baslik: Scalable Extraction of Training Data from (Production) Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It showed that large amounts of training data can be extracted even from aligned production models such as ChatGPT.

calismalar.baslik: Benchmark Data Contamination of Large Language Models: A Survey
calismalar.gerekce: It is a comprehensive survey of methods for detecting and mitigating benchmark contamination.

calismalar.baslik: Investigating Data Contamination in Modern Benchmarks for Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: Its TS-Guessing protocol found that models such as GPT-4 can guess hidden options in benchmarks like MMLU.

calismalar.baslik: Generalization or Memorization: Data Contamination and Trustworthy Evaluation for Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It proposed CDD, which detects contamination from the output distribution alone, together with the TED trustworthy-evaluation method.

calismalar.baslik: A Careful Examination of Large Language Model Performance on Grade School Arithmetic
calismalar.gerekce: Using the new GSM1k set, it measured overfitting to GSM8K and the resulting drop in performance.

calismalar.baslik: Data Contamination: From Memorization to Exploitation
calismalar.gerekce: It was an early controlled study of how contamination in pretraining is exploited on downstream tasks.

calismalar.baslik: Did the Neurons Read your Book? Document-level Membership Inference for Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It introduced document-level membership inference for copyrighted books and papers.

calismalar.baslik: DE-COP: Detecting Copyrighted Content in Language Models Training Data
calismalar.gerekce: It detects copyrighted content in training data with a multiple-choice test that asks the model to pick the verbatim passage among paraphrases.

calismalar.baslik: Copyright Traps for Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It proposed injecting trap sequences into documents in advance so that their later use in training can be detected.

calismalar.baslik: Privacy Risk in Machine Learning: Analyzing the Connection to Overfitting
calismalar.gerekce: It formalized the link between membership inference and overfitting and introduced the loss-threshold attack.

calismalar.baslik: Deduplicating Training Data Mitigates Privacy Risks in Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It showed that data duplication drives memorization and membership-inference success, and that deduplication is an effective defense.

calismalar.baslik: Membership Inference Attacks Cannot Prove that a Model Was Trained On Your Data
calismalar.gerekce: It showed that membership inference cannot provide legally sound proof of training-data use, and recommends data canaries and similar alternatives.

calismalar.baslik: LiveBench: A Challenging, Contamination-Free LLM Benchmark
calismalar.gerekce: It is a leading continuously updated benchmark designed to prevent contamination.

calismalar.baslik: LiveCodeBench: Holistic and Contamination Free Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code
calismalar.gerekce: It made contamination measurable for code by evaluating models on problems published after their training cutoff.

calismalar.baslik: Leak, Cheat, Repeat: Data Contamination and Evaluation Malpractices in Closed-Source LLMs
calismalar.gerekce: It documented indirect data leakage from closed-source models through user interactions, and related problems in evaluation practice.

calismalar.baslik: Scaling Up Membership Inference: When and How Attacks Succeed on Large Language Models
calismalar.gerekce: It showed that membership inference becomes effective when aggregated at the document and collection level.
